intro: Arkansas Legislative Audit examines every county and publishes what it finds. This page quotes what the auditors reported about Hot Spring County, from its latest report — no verdict added in either direction. What the auditors said is the record; what to make of it is yours.
regulatory_basis_note: Read this before reading any Arkansas audit: county and city reports carry a technical 'adverse opinion' on GAAP grounds because Arkansas law has them keep books on a simpler 'regulatory basis.' That phrase appears in every such audit in the state and signals the accounting format — not wrongdoing. A report is 'clean' or not in its findings, deficiencies, and noncompliance sections, which is what this page quotes.

verdicts.quote: During our evaluation, nothing came to our attention that would warrant disclosure in this report.
verdicts.detail: A limited review (a “financial and compliance report”), not a full audit: the financial statements in it are unaudited.

limits: From the 2024 report, dated May 7, 2026. Read by machine from the report’s text; the quotes are the auditors’ words. Older reports, and the separate federal (single) audits, aren’t on this page yet.
Arkansas alternates between full audits and limited “financial and compliance” reviews; each line says which this is.

cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the office of Mayor. cities.name: Perla
cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the office of Mayor. Mayor Total disbursements for the General Fund in 2023 exceeded appropriations by $25,595 (32%), in noncompliance with Ark. Code Ann. §14-58-203.

cities.name: Rockport
cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the offices of Mayor and District Court Clerk. Mayor In March 2024, the City disbursed $5,000 to the Police Chief, who stated this amount was for “comp time” earned. However, the City does not have a policy regarding paying officers for comp time. The Police Chief's comp time balance decreased in March 2024, after the City disbursed payment, and returned to the prior balance in April 2024, when the Police Chief reimbursed the City $5,000 in cash, which was deposited in the General Fund.
